solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old-fashioned drunk, say, outside holding forelock

indicators.note: holding means the outer pair of letters wraps around the forelock word
only the outside letters of the word say are used, the first and last

parts.note: a quiff is a tuft of hair brushed up over the forehead, a forelock

explanation.surface: Someone describes a tipsy person in dated terms, mentioning their forelock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example', but its outside letters S and Y hold QUIFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Squiffy is a dated British slang word meaning slightly tipsy or intoxicated.

clue.text: Search one working for the answer to this!

parts.note: a quest is a search
I is the Roman numeral for one
on means working, as a machine is switched on

explanation.surface: A searcher is set to work hunting for a solution.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: an answer is what you give in reply to an enquiry, so the thing this clue's answer responds to is the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An answer is a reply to an enquiry, so the thing being answered is a playful definition here.

clue.text: Single container must cover end of wage freeze

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single

indicators.note: covering something means enclosing it, so the cup wraps the letter

parts.note: a cup is a container

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of wage

explanation.surface: A pay freeze reduced to one cup of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freeze' looks like part of the wage-freeze picture, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice up is to become covered in ice, that is to freeze over.

clue.text: Angle on profit from such fabric

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after the first piece

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line
net profit, what is left after costs

explanation.surface: An angler makes money from a type of material.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishnet is an open mesh fabric used for stockings and tights.

clue.text: Makes changes to repairs on article

indicators.note: on here says the repairs word goes with the article attached in front

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
mends means repairs

explanation.surface: Someone alters repairs carried out on a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend a text is to make changes or corrections to it.

clue.text: Developing remit as experts

indicators.note: developing suggests changing form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remit grows as specialists take charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Developing' rearranges REMIT AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestri, plural of maestro, are masters or distinguished experts, especially in music.

clue.text: Cast gains a lot from dreams of home

indicators.note: cast in the sense of thrown about, so these letters are scattered and reformed

explanation.surface: The actors make large gains from their fantasies of home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a set of actors; it rearranges GAINS A LOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is a wistful longing for home or the past, literally homesickness.

clue.text: Slumped, unhappy eating scrambled egg

indicators.note: eating means the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: sad means unhappy

indicators.note: scrambled, like eggs, signals that the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone sat slumped and miserable over a plate of scrambled egg.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures breakfast; 'scrambled' is the signal to mix the letters, and 'eating' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagged means drooped or sank down, the same as slumped.

clue.text: Averse to change between sides in volte-face

indicators.note: between means the rearranged letters sit within the two side letters

parts.note: right and left are the two sides, R and L

indicators.note: to change signals that the letters of averse are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to alter their stance between two camps makes a U-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sides' supplies the two letters right and left, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A volte-face is a complete about-turn of opinion, a reversal.

clue.text: Support a hospital — finally bid cash

parts.note: a leg is a support, as of a table

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of hospital

parts.note: a tender is a formal bid for a contract

explanation.surface: Someone backing a hospital ends up making a cash offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal tender is money that must be accepted in payment, that is cash.

clue.text: Officer a lot of wardens ignore

indicators.note: a lot of means a large run of letters is taken from inside the words

explanation.surface: An officer disregards most of the prison staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'wardens ignore'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a junior commissioned officer, especially in the navy.

clue.text: Arrest made by head of security in front of tent

indicators.note: in front of places the security letter before the tent word
head of picks the first letter of security

parts.note: a big top is a circus tent, shortened here to top

explanation.surface: A security chief detains someone outside a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrest' as a verb means halt, not detain by police.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest something is to halt it, as in arresting decline.

clue.text: Bad experiences getting right names wrong

indicators.note: getting names wrong suggests the letters come out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone has an awful time after misremembering people's names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges RIGHT NAMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightmares, besides bad dreams, are any frightening or awful experiences.

clue.text: Anticipating long life, star played around

indicators.note: played around suggests messing about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A celebrity who fooled around looks forward to living long.
explanation.definitionFit: Forestalling means acting in advance to prevent something, anticipating it.

clue.text: The writer's back — crazy, pinching hotel cheese!

indicators.note: is back means the writer word is read backwards

parts.note: the writer means me, the setter; the 's here stands for is

indicators.note: pinching means taking something into its grip, so mental holds the letter

parts.note: mental means crazy
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone returns wildly to find a hotel has stolen their cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writer' is the setter, giving ME; the 's stands for 'is', so 'is back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmenthal is a Swiss cheese known for its large holes.

clue.text: Supporter present for victory in Europe in period before Christmas

indicators.note: for means one thing stands in for another, a swap

parts.note: Advent is the church season leading up to Christmas
VE as in VE Day, Victory in Europe
here means present, as in a roll-call

explanation.surface: A fan is around in the weeks leading up to Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' says HERE replaces VE in ADVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower or supporter of a cause or person.

clue.text: Parts of computers showing maternal love in poets?

parts.note: maternal means of a mother

indicators.note: in means the love letter goes inside the poets word

parts.note: bards are poets
love is zero in tennis scoring, hence the letter O

explanation.surface: Poets are shown expressing a mother's affection.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests verse about mothers.
explanation.definitionFit: Motherboards are the main circuit boards inside computers.

clue.text: Announce correct time, welcoming parliamentarian

indicators.note: welcoming means taking someone in, so true holds the member

parts.note: true means correct
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone declares the exact hour as a politician arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet something is to proclaim or announce it loudly.

clue.text: Mad dog could be!

definitions.meaning: ..., short for ... mad, is British slang for crazy
a dog could be making its characteristic noise

explanation.definitionFit: Barking is a British slang word meaning completely mad, and also what a dog does.

clue.text: Chicken or fish (flipping uncooked inside!)

indicators.note: inside means the flipped word goes within the fish

parts.note: a cod is a fish

indicators.note: flipping means turned over, so uncooked is read backwards

parts.note: raw means uncooked

explanation.surface: Choosing between chicken and fish, the cook finds it raw in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' looks like a menu choice beside fish, but as a noun it means a coward.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken is slang for a fearful person, a coward.

clue.text: Enter middle age in a state of unconsciousness, facing bankruptcy

parts.note: to go in is to enter

indicators.note: middle picks the central letter of age

parts.note: under means anaesthetised, as in being put under

explanation.surface: Someone reaches middle age, passes out, and faces financial ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle age' looks like a life stage but gives G, the middle of AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A business going under is failing, about to collapse into bankruptcy.

clue.text: Speaking lines, actors might need them

indicators.note: speaking means the word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: queues are lines of people waiting

explanation.surface: Actors may need prompts to deliver their lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' looks like an actor's script, but means queues.
explanation.definitionFit: Cues are signals telling actors when to speak or enter.

clue.text: Panic a detective arresting soldier in training

indicators.note: arresting means holding, so the answer is held within the words

explanation.surface: A panicking investigator detains a recruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters span 'Panic a detective'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a young trainee in the armed forces or police.

clue.text: Nearly closed inside — better count takings

indicators.note: inside means the shortened word goes within the next word

parts.note: to cap is to better, outdo

indicators.note: nearly means the word is cut short of its last letter

parts.note: shut means closed

explanation.surface: With the shop almost shut, it is time to tally the till.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is a verb here: to cap someone is to outdo them.
explanation.definitionFit: To cash up is to count the day's takings at closing time.

clue.text: Harness expensive-sounding beast

parts.note: a rein is part of a horse's harness

indicators.note: sounding means the word is heard rather than read, giving a different spelling

parts.note: dear means expensive

explanation.surface: A costly animal is put in harness.
explanation.definitionFit: A reindeer is an Arctic deer, a large beast of the north.

clue.text: Expand in elaborate detail

indicators.note: elaborate suggests working over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone goes into fuller, more elaborate detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elaborate' looks like an adjective, but it rearranges DETAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilate is to widen or expand; also to speak at length on a topic.

clue.text: Volunteers in a cottage in France cause trouble

indicators.note: in means the volunteers go within the cottage word

parts.note: a gite is a French holiday cottage
the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Volunteer soldiers stay in a French cottage and stir up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, the Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to stir up unrest or campaign disruptively.
